title: Virendra Kumar v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Dilip Gupta, J.; Mukhtar Ahmad, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; petitioner left to clause 6.5 bill objection.
headnote: A writ that only disputes the amount of a U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. bill is disposed of by leaving the petitioner to file an objection under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The Court did not examine the billed amount on merits.
facts: Virendra Kumar filed a writ petition in the Allahabad High Court against the State of Uttar Pradesh and others, including U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. He disputed the amount shown in a bill raised by the Corporation. A Division Bench of Dilip Gupta and Mukhtar Ahmad JJ. heard the matter on 10 March 2016. The Court did not test whether the billed figure was correct and instead pointed the petitioner to the statutory objection route under the Supply Code.

holding_units.holding: A consumer who disputes only the amount indicated in a bill raised by the licensee must pursue an objection under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; a writ raising that dispute is disposed of by leaving the petitioner to that remedy.

not_decided.note: The Court did not examine the bill on merits and left the petitioner to a clause 6.5 objection.
